newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH share falls, brokers cut forecasts.
newsitem.headline: LVMH share falls, brokers cut forecasts.

text.p: Shares in luxury goods conglomerate LVMH were down sharply on Thursday as several brokers cut their earnings estimates for the group after studying its first-half results.

LVMH said profit rose 5.4 percent in the first half of 1996 to 1.54 billion francs but operating income fell to 2.61 billion francs from 2.92 billion due to a sharp fall in profit in its perfumes and cosmetics division.
"Their numbers are disappointing. We'll probably revise our estimate down for 1996. The 1997 estimate could also come down slightly," said analyst Cedric Magnelia at CS First Boston.
He said he would probably reduce his 1996 estimate from a profit of 4.4 billion francs to a figure close to last year's profit excluding exceptionals of 4.05 billion francs.
Two analysts at French brokerage houses left their profit estimates at around 4.4 billion francs for 1996.
LVMH shares were down 1.73 percent at 1,082 francs at 1100 GMT after recovering from a session low of 1,057.
The company said operating income at its perfumes division slid to 70 million francs from 380 million, reflecting its battle to keep its prestigious perfumes off the gray market.

Analyst Sylvain Massot at Morgan Stanley said he was slashing his 1996 profit growth estimate to five percent from 10 percent. He said he would trim his 1997 forecast to show growth of about seven percent, instead of 10 percent previously.
"Previously we had a letdown with the volumes. Now it's the margins that are disappointing despite currency hedging," he said.
He said the solid performance of the other divisions was due in large part to shrewd currency hedging for this year, namely on the Japanese yen, that will not be in effect in 1997.
CSFB's Magnelia said a question mark hung over the fourth quarter because of weak consumption in Europe, but he said he was more confident looking out on a two-to-three year horizon.
"There are growth opportunities for Louis Vuitton in Asia, cognac is doing better and the champagnes look fine," he said.
